5742fbd32b.q: How should health tech founders navigate reimbursement and payer incentives when building products in regulated healthcare?
5742fbd32b.a: Successful players figure out a lane where they are not necessarily fighting the system but aligning with the interests of the party who is carrying the cost. The real big boss is reimbursement, not FDA approval. Your product is dead in the water even if it clears FDA if you skip reimbursement and what payers care about—like whether you reduce their cost or improve their efficiency.

05a32325e7.q: What is the Advisory 5 methodology for turning reflection into action for founders?
05a32325e7.a: In Advisory 5 methodology, an action is not writing a business plan—it is doing something that gets the possibility of getting a no. Examples include asking a pilot customer to become permanent, making an ask of an investor, or doing something outside your comfort zone. The challenge is creating a space where action is the outcome of reflection, not just staying in the comfortable space of learning.

55a53657d8.q: How does Garner Health align incentives with employers in the healthcare benefits space?
55a53657d8.a: Garner Health works directly with employers who offer benefits to employees. They track metrics across thousands of physicians and millions of claims to see where those metrics produce the best outcomes. They help cover out-of-pocket expenses for going to the top provider, resulting in at least 12% savings for the employer without changing or touching the existing plan.
